summary.title: Write a shell in C
summary.one_liner: You learn how a basic Unix shell works by building a read-eval loop in C that reads input, tokenizes it with strtok, and runs commands via fork and execvp.
keywords: how does a terminal shell work
takeaways: A shell is a loop that prints a prompt, reads a line, splits it into tokens, and executes them.
Dynamic input reading uses malloc and realloc, doubling the buffer as needed, since command length is unknown in advance.
strtok splits the line on delimiters; the first call takes the string and later calls pass NULL.
fork creates a child process; the child calls execvp to replace itself with the command, and the parent waits with waitpid.
The exit builtin is handled in code by returning 0 to end the loop, since it cannot be run as an external program.
summary.summary: The article walks through writing a minimal shell named "dash" in C. It covers the main loop with a > prompt, reading input with a growing buffer using malloc and realloc, and tokenizing with strtok. Command execution uses fork, execvp, and waitpid, and exit is handled as a special builtin that ends the loop. The full source code for the basic shell is included, and the author notes it is a learning exercise rather than a production tool.
